steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Grease a muffin pan or line with paper liners.

Cream together butter and brown sugar in a large bowl with an electric mixer on medium speed until fluffy. Add mashed bananas, eggs, milk, and vanilla; mix well. Stir in flour, bran, baking powder, baking soda, and salt; blend just until moistened. Stir in walnuts. Pour batter into the prepared muffin cups.

Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into the center of a muffin comes out clean, 20 to 25 minutes. Cool muffins in the pan for 5 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.

raw_recipe.headline: Banana Bran Muffins
raw_recipe.description: This banana bran muffin recipe is easy to make with wheat bran cereal, crunchy walnuts, and lots of ripe bananas for a healthy breakfast or snack.
raw_recipe.name: Banana Bran Muffins

review.reviewBody: I was looking for a lower fat/calorie banana bran muffin so I modified this in combination with another low fat bran muffin recipe. I substituted the butter for 1/4c unsweetened applesauce, only used 1 egg, halved the sugar to 1/4c, increased the wheat bran to 1c and used 1/2c each of wheat flour and all purpose flour. The sweetness was just perfect for me (the banana gives a lot of sweet flavor) and so moist! Each muffin turns out to be about 100 calories, so we're free to munch on them guiltless! The first batch I made used only 2 bananas and 1/2c applesauce, this was a little dryer than using 3 bananas and 1/4c applesauce, but still good!

So lovely as a high fiber low calorie muffin. I did take some suggestions. Added some spices (cinnamon, ginger, allspice, nutmeg) and also wanted additional bran so did half and half 1 cup wheat bran 1 cup flour. I also added a crumble cause..why not? it felt right. But it was such a nice touch. (1/3 cup brown sugar; 2 tbls flour; 1/4 tsp cinnamon; 1 tbls butter) sprinkle. For extra big muffin tops i let the mixture sit for around 15 minutes. Fill tins to the top. Alternate tins to leave more space for bigger muffins. Bake at 425⁰ for first 7 minutes and drop down to 350⁰ for the remaining cooking time (12 minutes) let cool 10 min before moving to cooling rack. Deeeeelicious

2nd bake update. I made this recipe again a week after my first. I made these changes: 1. As I did the first time, I subbed in Greek yogurt for buttermilk- partly because it offers more protein 2.- I used two cups of Raisin Bran, not four (I did this the first time too and should have mentioned it) 3. Added 1 teaspoon of vanilla extract and a dash of cinnamon along with a handful of chopped up mixed unsalted nuts. I bake these in a small conventional oven with a double rack, let cool, then freeze . Microwave for 20-30 seconds and enjoy whenever.

Great base recipe. I used a stand mixer to mix everything really well before adding dry ingredients - no need to pre-mash bananas. Subbed out whole wheat flour, added 2 TBS flax, 1/4 c. nutritional yeast, 1TBS maca, ground cardamom (a few sprinkles), forgot the walnuts, and increased milk to 1/2 c because of added dry ingredients. Baked as mini muffins for a quick healthy snack. A+

I gave this a 4 because I made some variations. Very moist, great texture and very tasty muffins. I doubled this recipe and added 1/2c. flax seed meal, 1/4c. Chia seeds (grounded up) 2 tsp. all spice and 1 tsp. cinnamon. I also soaked the bran in the milk and added an extra 1/4c. milk (for added moisture because I added the extra flax and chia) I also did 2c. whole wheat flour and 1c. All purpose flour. (I usually take 1/2 butter and replace it with applesauce but didn't have any this time.) I didn't add the nuts as I wanted to send these to school for the kids lunches. Made 3/4 of the recipe plain and added Chocolate chips to the last portion. These Were Great. Will be keeping this recipe.

I used the basic recipe but made a few modifications. I added two additional tablespoons of butter; 1/4 c peanut butter protein, and 1.5 tablespoons of cocoa. They were amazing. I will definitely keep this recipe.
Next time I am going to substitute monk fruit sweetener for some of the brown sugar.

This is a staple in my house. I did modify the flour ratios to minimize the all-purpose flour: 3/4 c. all-purpose flour, 3/4 c. coconut flour, 3/4 c. Wheat bran. Tastes great and makes my digestive system happy!
Great recipe, I cut down butter and sugar but increased banana and added zest of one orange. Also changed it to one cup bran and one cup flour. They turned out to be delicious!
Added 1/2 cup crushed bran flakes 1/2 cup whole wheat flour, cut all purpose flour back to 1 cup. Used apple sauce instead of butter
Fiancé and I loved them! I didn’t have any milk so substituted for equal part Greek yogurt (no sugar added, plain, 0%). Came our super fluffy and moist.

This is a great base recipe. Initially made as written and very good, but I now use this as a base for wet/dry ingredients and have made it much more healthy. I sub applesauce for the oil/butter, sub ground oatmeal for the flour, and ground flax seed for the bran. I also use a bit less than 1/4 cup honey in place of the sugar. I double the recipe and freeze the muffins individually for a quick breakfast.
These were good and I made them exactly how the recipe said. I will say there was almost no sweetness to them. I think I’m going to add a touch more sugar next time
No walnuts, so I added in raisins and pumpkin seeds. The pumpkin seeds were tasty bit of crunchiness. I had to hide some for tomorrow.

I've made these twice now. They are perfect. This time I only had 2 bananas so I used a cup of finely chopped fresh pineapple ( left out the milk because my batter was wet enough), and added a palm full of shredded coconut to boot. Fantastic tropical banana nut muffins.
I used flaxmeal instead of wheat bran and instead of walnuts I used chocolate chips. They were light and fluffy and golden brown. Delicious

I just ate one from the oven. It was so worthy of dessert! I used half bran, half flour and added, about 1/4 cup each walnuts, unsweetened coconut-and 1/4 cup raisins. Also did not measure but sprinkled a bunch of flax seed, ground ginger, cinnamon and a touch of turmeric. They are so delicious with fluffy texture. Next time, I’ll cut the sugar and perhaps add more nuts or seeds. Between Banana, coconut and raisins, it pretty sweet. I may also increase ginger to balance sweet with a tiny kick.
I used a cup o shredded wheat from the bottom of the cereal bag and less flour. I used some yogurt and less butter, sprinkled some of the shredded wheat on top as well. Very good.

I liked the basics of this recipe. I usually find a recipe and then make it my own. I one and a half times this recipe. I used sprouted whole wheat flour instead of white. I omitted butter and used half a cup of canola and one cup of applesauce. I also added one extra teaspoon of baking powder. Some people were saying their's didn't rise very well, so I added extra tsp and it turned out beautiful.
I made 6 jumbo muffins, at sea level baked 25 min @ 375. A little bland. Maybe a little more salt and tsp of orange or lemon zest, maybe a little nutmeg.
The only thing I did different is used whipping cream instead of milk. I had a bit to use up. They are really moist and delicious.
